title: Jared Carter is sent east again with the Comforter as guide
setting: Jared Carter had spent late 1831 and early 1832 preaching in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, and Vermont. A few weeks after returning home to Amherst, Ohio, he went to Hiram. There he asked Joseph Smith what the Lord wanted for his next season of preaching. Joseph dictated this revelation on 12 March 1832. Carter left on the new mission on 15 April 1832.
summary: The revelation tells Jared Carter to go again into the eastern countries. He is to preach from city to city by the authority of his ordination. It promises to send the Comforter to teach him the truth and where to go. If he is faithful, he will be crowned “again with sheaves.” It tells him to let his heart be glad and not to fear. The speaker names himself as Jesus Christ.

contextNote.title: A guide for a route not yet chosen
contextNote.text: Carter came to Hiram asking where and how to preach next. Verse 1 sets only the region: the “eastern countries,” from place to place. Verse 2 leaves the details to the Comforter, who will teach him the way he should go. Verse 3 looks back on his earlier mission with the word “again.” Sheaves are bundles of harvested grain, an image of converts gathered in. In this passage, the Comforter is a guide for the journey as well as a teacher of truth.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 77–80, “I Will Lead You Along,” shows the Lord guiding servants like Jared Carter. What does verse 2 promise Jared Carter about the choices the revelation itself leaves open?

reviewNote: Read all 4 verses. Heading gives Hiram, 12 March 1832. JSP historical introduction gives Carter’s prior missions, his trip from Amherst to ask about his ministry, and his 15 April 1832 departure. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
